page.layout: One printed page, text only. Running head at top with page number 109 at top right. Heading "Ex Graeco Simonidis." centred, then a poem of 14 lines in two-line stanzas, then heading "E Graeco Theognidis." centred, then a second poem of 6 lines. Both poems have large initial letters (R and N). An ornamental tailpiece below the second poem. No marginal notes.

l.i: REbus in humanis nulla eft conftantia certa,
Veridico vates Chius vt ore canit.
Non minus eft foliis hominum gens fluxa
caducis: Pauci vbi coeperunt auribus ifta fuis
Pectoribus fixere: animis namque indita
quondam Spes teneris blandè credula corda fouet.
Et dum laeta viret foecundo flore iuuenta
Percurfant animos irrita multa leues.
Nec fenium mortem ve patet, neque corpore fano
Prouida ventura cura doloris adeft.
O malè ftultorum mens credula, qui breuis aui
Tempora non norint quàm fugitiua volent.
At tu praemonitus nigrae ad confinia mortis,
Laetus age, & genio gratificare tuo.
NEmo meam cumulet violis fragrātibus
vrnā, Nec mihi Pyramidū mole sepulchra
locet. Si quis amat vino largum se praestet amicum,
Talibus officiis dum locus esse potest.
Verum vbi consumptos Lachesis mihi finiet
annos, Vel fracta inculris horreat vrna rubis.

page.notes: The first letters R and N are large decorative initials, joined to the words Ebus and Emo as read. The line "Non minus eft foliis hominum gens fluxa caducis:" and similar lines are printed as in the scan. Printed spelling kept, including "Pectoribus", "foecundo", "fano", "rubis" and "conftantia". Italic throughout the poems. The tailpiece ornament is not text and is not transcribed. Some words are lightly blurred ("inculris", "vrnā") and may need checking against the original.
